title: The white elephant dream
hookLine: Queen Maya dreams a white elephant enters her side; the wise men say a great son is coming
last: THE DHAMMAPADA — WHAT YOU THINK, YOU BECOME.

lines: A QUEEN DREAMS OF AN ELEPHANT.
cards: Night, in Kapilavatthu, a city at the foot of the Himalayas. It's the time of a summer festival. Queen Maya, wife of King Suddhodana, has kept the festival well, given gifts, and gone to sleep.
She dreams that a white elephant, shining like silver, walks toward her, circles her bed, and enters her side. The Buddha's life story begins here, one scene at a time.

teach.b: In the later tellings, guardian spirits carry Maya up to a high place in the mountains, bathe her in a lake, and lay her on a heavenly couch.

teach.h: SIX TUSKS AND A WHITE LOTUS.
teach.b: A white elephant with six tusks, a white lotus in its trunk, comes down from a golden mountain, trumpets, walks around her three times, and seems to enter her right side.
In the morning she tells the king. He calls in the brahmins, the wise men who read signs. Be glad, they say.

The queen has conceived, and it's a son. If he stays in the household, he'll be a great king who rules the world. If he leaves it, he'll be a buddha: one who wakes up and removes the veil from the world.
Where does this come from? The early discourses describe his conception with wonders, a great light, the earth trembling, but no elephant.

teach.h: A LATER TELLING, CARVED IN STONE.
teach.b: The dream comes from later biographies and commentaries, and it's old in its own right: the scene is carved in stone at early Buddhist sites in India, such as Bharhut. Why an elephant?
In ancient India a white elephant was a royal treasure, rare and auspicious: strength, gentleness and greatness at once.

Across Buddhist Asia the dream is painted on temple walls, and in Thailand and Myanmar the white elephant is still a sign of blessing. Before anyone knows who this child will be, something announces him.

how: Buddhists remember Maya's dream in temple murals, carvings and festival plays; in many countries the story is told to children as the first chapter of the Buddha's life, and the white elephant remains a symbol of blessing.

o: the animal the prince rode when he left home
Maya's dream sign that a great son was coming
a gift too costly to keep, as the English saying goes

games.q: you're King Suddhodana. your queen has dreamed a white elephant entered her side. what do you do?
o: ignore it. it's only a dream.
call the wise men to read it.
send the queen away to rest.
games.why: he calls the brahmins. they tell him to be glad: a son is coming, who will be a great king, or, if he leaves home, a buddha.

practice: From today, the bell gives you two minutes. Sit comfortably and recall a dream that stayed with you, from childhood or from last month: its colors, the place, the feeling when you woke.
Don't decide what it meant; some things arrive in us before we understand them, and when the mind wanders, come back to the breath.

wordCard.voice: White elephant. Queen Maya's dream before the birth: six tusks, a white lotus, and a son who would be a king or a buddha.

carryVoice: Your line: some things announce themselves. Tomorrow, the child arrives, in a garden on the road. That's camp two, day one.
